chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The squatting (ihtiba') is disliked for the one in Ihram, and it is disliked in the Sacred Masjid.

key_terms.الِاحْتِبَاءُ: A specific posture of sitting or squatting with knees drawn up to the chest.
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on squatting (ihtiba') for a pilgrim in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific etiquette (adab) for the pilgrim in Ihram, prohibiting the posture of 'ihtiba''—squatting with knees drawn to the chest—as a disliked act (makruh) within the precincts of the Sacred Mosque. This ruling underscores the reverence due to the Kaaba, distinguishing the general prohibitions of Ihram from the heightened decorum required in the holiest site, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on maintaining dignity and focus during worship.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The squatting (الِاحْتِبَاءُ) is disliked for the one in Ihraam, and it is disliked in the Sacred Masjid’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is undesirable for one in the state of Ihram to sit in Masjid al-Haram facing al-Ka‘bah in al-‘Ihtiba’ position (with one’s knees raised and legs against thighs with hips on the ground).”’
